issues.description: install.sh minimum-version check still accepts Python 3.7-3.9 while error message says >= 3.10
issues.detail: install.sh prints 'Chia requires Python version >= 3.10 and < 3.13.0' but the actual predicate still reads `[ "$PYTHON_MINOR_VER" -lt "7" ]`. The implementation contract disagrees with the user-facing message: 3.7/3.8/3.9 will silently pass this gate and fail later at pip install time with a worse error. Tighten the numeric guard to `-lt 10` so the check matches the stated floor. Also consider dropping the bare `3` from the find_python search loop so a stray `python3 -> 3.9` doesn't satisfy the probe.

issues.description: Ruff UP007/UP035/UP045 globally suppressed with a bare TODO — contradicts the PR's stated PEP 604 migration
issues.detail: ruff.toml adds UP045, UP007, UP035 to the global ignore list with the comment 'TODO: Remove these - it's a lot of errors.' These are exactly the Union/Optional -> `A | B`/`A | None` rules the PR description names as the motivating cleanup. Either land the mechanical autofix in this PR (`ruff check --fix --select UP007,UP035,UP045`) or replace the TODO with a tracked issue that has an owner and a kill date. A bare TODO disabling the rule you say you're enforcing will become permanent style debt.

issues.description: default_raise() sentinel and its '< 3.10 compatibility' comment are stale after dropping 3.9
issues.detail: wallet_request_types.py keeps `default_raise()` with `# pragma: no cover` and the comment 'just for < 3.10 compatibility', used as `field(default_factory=default_raise)` on many request dataclasses. With kw_only=True now unconditional, these fields should simply be required kw-only fields without a default; the factory-that-raises is a runtime trap where the constructor could refuse the program directly. Either delete default_raise and let the dataclass machinery enforce required fields, or — if streamable forces defaults — rename it and rewrite the comment to state the real current rationale.

issues.description: test-install-scripts.yml runs gratuitous `dnf update -y` and `dnf search python3.12` diagnostic noise in install steps
issues.detail: The Amazon Linux and Rocky prep steps now run `dnf update -y && dnf search python3.12 && dnf install git python3.12 -y`. `dnf search` is a human-facing discovery command whose output is never consumed or asserted on — pure log noise. `dnf update -y` on every CI run churns the image, slows the matrix, and changes the test baseline between runs. The minimal correct form is `dnf install -y git python3.12`. If diagnostics are wanted, make them a separate, documented step.

issues.description: kw_only_dataclass helper inlined into ~15 identical decorator stacks instead of kept as one named concept
issues.detail: The PR deletes the `kw_only_dataclass` helper and replaces it with `@dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True)` repeated on roughly fifteen classes. The version-guard inside the helper was the problem, not the helper itself — the named decorator encoded a project convention ('streamable request types are frozen kw-only dataclasses'). Restore a thin one-line helper (without the version branch) so future readers see the intent and a single edit (e.g., adding slots=True) touches one site rather than fifteen.

issues.description: conditions.py drops `# pragma: no cover` without confirming the branch is actually covered on 3.10+
issues.detail: The 3.9-coverage-quirk comment and pragma were removed from parse_timelock_info, leaving a bare `continue` in an elif chain. The removal is correct in spirit, but the change presumes the existing test suite now exercises this branch. Either confirm coverage holds on supported versions, add a one-line comment explaining the 'ignore unrelated condition types' intent, or replace the bare continue with an assert/raise to fail loudly when a new Condition subclass is added without updating this function.

issues.description: cmd_classes.py option() default semantics shifted from None-fallback to MISSING without an audit of call sites
issues.detail: With 3.9 removed, `default=kwargs.get('default', MISSING)` is now the correct expression, but the pre-3.10 code distinguished MISSING from None because older dataclasses couldn't express 'no default with kw_only'. The diff doesn't show that callers of option() were audited for the semantic shift from None-as-sentinel back to MISSING. Worth a grep to confirm no call site relied on the old None default.

issues.description: itertools.pairwise swap is a clean, unrelated cleanup bundled into a version-drop PR
issues.detail: Replacing `zip(ordered, ordered[1:])` with `itertools.pairwise(ordered)` is correct and only valid on 3.10+. It is, however, opportunistic cleanup unrelated to 'remove Python 3.9 support'; bundling unrelated edits into a version-drop PR makes the diff harder to bisect and revert. Not a defect — the swap is the right call — and worth applying repo-wide as a follow-up. A one-line invariant comment on this test helper would not hurt.

synthesis.summary: The mechanical 3.9 removal is competent and the architectural direction is right — kw_only=True is now unconditional, sys.version_info branches are gone, and the kw_only_dataclass version-guard is correctly retired. But the cleanup stops short of the simplification it enables and contradicts its own stated goals in two places. First, ruff.toml globally suppresses UP007/UP035/UP045 with a bare TODO — exactly the Union/Optional -> PEP 604 rules the PR description names as motivation. Second, default_raise() lives on as a runtime-trap factory with a stale '< 3.10 compatibility' comment, when with kw_only=True the fields should simply be required. Smaller drift: install.sh tells users '>= 3.10' but the numeric check still accepts 3.7+, CI install steps ship `dnf update -y && dnf search python3.12` diagnostic noise, the kw_only_dataclass helper was inlined into fifteen identical decorator stacks instead of kept (minus the version branch), and a `# pragma: no cover` was dropped without confirming coverage now holds. Verdict: needs-work — fix the install.sh floor check, drop the CI search/update noise, and either land the PEP 604 codemod or scope the ruff ignore behind a tracked owner.
